Change Details: Dropped 13 columns that are 100% empty (e.g. host_since, host_response_rate, instant_bookable).
Reason and Justification: These fields are not populated in the June 2026 Sydney snapshot, so they carry no information.

Change Details: Removed 2,787 listings with no nightly price (17,786 remain).
Reason and Justification: Price is the key outcome for Q2, Q3, A3 and all models. Listings without a price are mostly unbookable or inactive.

Change Details: Removed 1,778 listings with minimum stay above 30 nights (16,008 remain).
Reason and Justification: These are mid/long-term rentals (most require 90+ nights). They price and book differently from short-term stays.

Change Details: Removed 322 listings priced below $65 or above $2,979 per night (1st/99th percentiles).
Reason and Justification: The raw maximum was over $50,000 a night, which looks like data entry errors or placeholder prices. Trimming stops a few points dominating means and regressions.

Change Details: Filled 1,221 missing bathroom counts by parsing bathrooms_text; added a shared-bathroom flag.
Reason and Justification: The text field holds the same information (e.g. '1.5 shared baths'), so parsing recovers values without guessing.

Change Details: Imputed missing bedrooms (2,060), beds (561) and bathrooms (15) with the median of listings with the same room type and capacity.
Reason and Justification: Guest capacity strongly predicts room counts. A grouped median keeps imputed values realistic and avoids dropping listings.

Change Details: Created amenities_count, superhost flag, property_group (top 6 types + Other), host_tier (1 / 2-9 / 10+ listings) and a 'rated' flag (5+ reviews).
Reason and Justification: These turn raw text and long-tail categories into variables the analysis and models can use. With fewer than 5 reviews a rating is too noisy to compare.

Change Details: Kept review-score gaps as missing (not imputed) for EDA; rating analyses use listings with 5+ reviews only.
Reason and Justification: 12.0% of listings have no rating because they have no reviews. Filling these in would invent guest opinions.

Change Details: External data: condensed the TfNSW GTFS timetable to 254 Sydney rail, Metro and light-rail stations (740 entrance points) with mode, off-peak frequency and rail travel time to the CBD and airport (External01).
Reason and Justification: Replaces the 2020 entrance file, which misses every station opened since 2020 (Metro City & Southwest, Parramatta Light Rail). Frequency and travel time measure the quality of rail access, not just its distance.

Change Details: Joined 12-month average station entries and exits (External02, 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-01) to stations by normalised name (99.2% of stations matched); 'Less than 50' set to 25.
Reason and Justification: Patronage indicates how busy and well-served a station is. Name formats differ between TfNSW files ('Central  Station' vs 'Central Station').

Change Details: Measured walking distance to the nearest entrance on the OpenStreetMap pedestrian network (99.9% of listings routed; the rest use straight-line distance x 1.343, the median detour). Distance bands now use walking distance.
Reason and Justification: Guests walk along streets, not in straight lines. Rivers, harbour inlets and rail corridors make some 'near' listings a long walk away.

Change Details: Placed each listing in its ABS SA2 (2021 boundaries) and attached the SA2's SEIFA IRSAD score (External03); added distance to the nearest named beach and the number of tourist attractions within 1 km (External04, OpenStreetMap).
Reason and Justification: SA2s are about 7x finer than LGAs, so they control for neighbourhood quality much more tightly. Beaches and attractions are the main reasons rail-remote areas (e.g. the Northern Beaches) are expensive.

Change Details: Kept the 2020 entrance file (External05) only as a comparison: 18 current stations are missing from it and 1,679 listings are more than 200 m closer to rail on the current network.
Reason and Justification: Shows how much measurement error the outdated network introduced; such error biases a rail effect towards zero.

Change Details: Summarised calendar.csv.gz to one row per listing: share of unavailable nights in the 90 days after 2026-06-29 (unavailable_rate_90d).
Reason and Justification: The calendar has 7.5 million daily rows and no price. A listing-level 90-day share is a usable forward demand signal. Note that 'unavailable' mixes real bookings with host-blocked nights.

Change Details: Prepared the 21 March 2026 snapshot (13,194 listings after the same cleaning) for a cross-season check; the September and December 2025 snapshots were not used.
Reason and Justification: The June snapshot is a winter snapshot; a March (late-summer) snapshot tests whether the rail result is seasonal. The 2025 snapshots have no prices.
